To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the complex natural resonances of concealed weapons can be excited and detected using a phased array antenna system.

the complex natural resonances of concealed items can be excited by ultra-wide-band stepped frequency continuous wave microwave illumination of the target and the late time transient response of the object can be spatially localized and used to identify and classify the concealed object, using a phased antenna array.
“The detection and identification of concealed handguns, knives, mobile phones and cameras using a phased antenna array, operating at 0.3-3 GHz, is feasible.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, non-invasive, concealed weapon detector.
the detection and identification of concealed weapons using a novel phased array of ultra wide band transmitters and receivers.

the development of a new generation of concealed weapon detection systems, based upon the use of ultra wideband, stepped frequency continuous illumination and phased array imaging techniques, which can be used in a wide range of security applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the detection, classification and imaging of metal objects of linear size ≥10 cm concealed upon the human form is entirely feasible, and can be achieved by using a phased antenna array, and a suitable signal processing algorithm, to process the received signals.
a phased array system is a feasible solution for the detection and identification of concealed objects, including weapons.

a phased array system is capable of detecting concealed objects of size greater than 10cm, and that the late time response can be used for classification of the threat object, so that the threat can be differentiated from a non-threat object.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a system that can detect concealed weapons, such as handguns and rifles, on the body of a person.

the use of ultra wideband stepped frequency continuous wave excitation of a phased array of ultra wide band antennae is an entirely feasible means for detecting and classifying concealed weapons on the human body.

the detection and identification of weapons and other metal items of linear dimension ≥ 10 cm concealed upon the human torso is entirely feasible by using an array of suitably wide band transceiver antennae, operating in the 300 MHz to 3 GHz band.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use a phased array to excite complex natural resonances of the concealed object and to spatially locate these complex natural resonances using a phased array.
a phased array antenna system, using a single transmitter/receiver pair, can detect concealed objects on the human body, and can also classify the object based on its natural resonance frequencies.
the late time response, which is the main focus of this invention, is a very robust and reliable feature that can be used to classify the concealed object.
